# Shared-target deploy proof must follow installed bytes

<a id="body"></a>

## Body

Add to the existing executable-lifetime notes: a successful build and correct version check do not bind a mutable shared-target pathname to the bytes subsequently installed.

Use two real temporary Git worktrees with fake cargo and private target/HOME/TMPDIR: A builds/checks, B builds through the same shared-build lock, then A installs. Assert the installed copy answers A's stamp while the shared target answers B's. This caught R271-001; copying to a private snapshot under the lock closed it. A FIFO as copy source lets a lightweight probe observe that cp has opened the source while the target lock still exists. No real cargo or fleet deploy is needed.

For dirty-input guards, follow production includes beyond crates/: claude_settings.rs embeds harness/scripts hooks; community/layout.rs embeds .dd/schemas/pij; community/templates.rs embeds templates/roles. Checking only crates/manifests/extension roots misses those inputs. Test interruption separately from returned errors: SIGTERM before the helper hands off its snapshot can leak a directory even when build/stamp/install error cleanup passes.

#271 final review: 8b08ba8f43726d7906076d4ef4fb2785f5472df9, verdict 01e9626640a326a369da70e53a29a0ca2a43729b. R271-001 closed; omitted embedded inputs and interrupted-snapshot cleanup were named nonblocking C34 follow-ups R271-002/R271-003, not a third review round.
